pageCache.pageTitle: Our size is our superpower. | Babington House
pageCache.text:
Our size is our superpower.
As a truly independent school, Babington is small enough to know and celebrate every child, yet big enough to unlock their potential, we provide a bespoke approach to education for pupils aged 3 to 16.
Within our close-knit community, every child is recognised as an individual — encouraged to grow in confidence, build meaningful friendships and discover their unique strengths.
Guided by our values, we inspire imagination, challenge thinking and nurture each child’s unique potential. We develop confident, curious and compassionate young people with the courage to embrace opportunities, discover their individuality and become the very best version of themselves.
Explore our Admissions process
Perfectly situated in the heart of Chislehurst
We are perfectly situated in the heart of Chislehurst being only 3 minutes walk from Elmstead Woods Station and within easy reach of Central London

Welcome to Babington House School
From the moment you walk through the doors of Babington House, you are met with a genuine sense of warmth and happiness, alongside a clear sense of aspiration and ambition.
Our co-educational setting creates a harmonious and balanced community that reflects the world beyond our gates. But it is our size that makes Babington truly special. In our close-knit community, every pupil is known, valued and encouraged to be themselves.
Being a smaller school also means that every child has the opportunity to play a full and active part in school life – whether performing on stage, representing the school in sport, creating in the art studio, making music or discovering a new passion. There really is something for everyone.
Our dynamic curriculum, extensive enrichment programme and exceptional staff give pupils the opportunity to discover what they love, challenge themselves and develop the confidence to fulfil their potential.
This year, Babington celebrates its 140th anniversary. We are proud of the heritage and traditions that have shaped our school, while looking firmly to the future. We are investing in new developments and inspiring facilities that support an innovative, student-centred education.
I am immensely proud to lead such a vibrant, welcoming and forward-thinking community. I hope our website gives you a flavour of what makes Babington special – but the best way to experience it is to come and see it for yourself.
I would be delighted to welcome you to Babington House and show you around.
Mr David Laird Headteacher
Headmaster’s Profile
David Laird brings over twenty-five years of experience in the education sector, having worked at some of the world’s leading independent, international, and boarding schools. Notable career highlights include his tenure as Principal of The British School of Beijing in China and his role as a boarding teacher at the prestigious Institut Le Rosey in Switzerland. In 2019, Mr. Laird founded The British School of Lisbon in Portugal, where he served as the inaugural Headmaster.
While Mr. Laird’s primary expertise lies in schools offering the English National Curriculum, he has also led an IB continuum school in central London. His pedagogical philosophy emphasises the importance of providing outstanding teaching and learning. At the same time, he is committed to creating unique opportunities for students that extend beyond the classroom, helping them develop as well-rounded global citizens who can adapt to an ever-changing world.
“Finding the right school for your child is so important and I think it is a place where they should be happy.”

pageCache.pageTitle: Early Years Curriculum | Nursery | Babington House
pageCache.text:
This is where their learning journey begins.
Our Nursery and Reception pupils become part of the Babington family from the moment they start. Set within our historic grounds, our newly renovated Nursery has been purposefully designed to inspire curiosity, imaginative play and discovery. Children can explore cosy reading areas, imaginative play zones, creative spaces, interactive learning areas and calm zones.
Our bespoke outdoor area extends learning beyond the classroom, with a garden, creative area and obstacle course where children can develop physical, practical and communication skills through play and exploration.
Early Years Learning
Our specialist Early Years teachers provide a carefully structured day built around the EYFS, with plenty of opportunities for play, creativity, curiosity, discovery – and most importantly, fun!
Our curriculum supports children’s development across the seven areas of learning, building the knowledge, skills and confidence they need for the next stage of their journey.
There are three prime areas which are:
Personal, social and emotional development Communication and language Physical development
There are four specific areas which are:
Understanding the world Literacy Mathematics Expressive arts and design
Phonics and Early Reading
Our carefully structured phonics programme begins in Nursery with Little Wandle and develops through Reception, supporting children as they explore sounds, develop early phonics skills and begin to read simple words.

pageCache.pageTitle: Investing in the future of our students – announcement from Mr Laird, Headteacher - Babington House
pageCache.text:
I am delighted to announce that our Governing Body has approved a significant programme of summer works at Babington House School. Representing an £800,000 commitment to enhancing our educational environment, these developments mark another important step in our ambition to create exceptional spaces where every pupil can learn, grow and thrive.
At the heart of this programme is the creation of the new Tim Lello Library and Study Centre. Developed over the summer, this inspiring new facility will provide pupils of all ages with a vibrant and purposeful environment for reading, independent study, research and collaboration.
Alongside this, we are pleased to be undertaking a full renovation of our Nursery, Reception and outdoor EYFS areas. These bespoke, state-of-the-art learning spaces are being thoughtfully designed around the needs of our youngest learners, with every detail carefully considered to support early childhood development. The new environments will encourage children to explore, investigate, collaborate and build confidence through play, discovery and high-quality teaching.
I am also delighted to announce that Mrs Hamilton will be joining our EYFS team as Reception Teacher at a particularly exciting time for the department. She brings a wealth of experience both in teaching and as a professional artist and we look forward to the creativity, expertise and enthusiasm she will bring to our youngest learners.
As Babington celebrates its 140th anniversary, we are proud to honour our rich heritage while continuing to invest in the future of our school community. These developments reflect our commitment to providing an innovative, student-centred education and ensuring that our pupils benefit from facilities that inspire ambition, creativity and intellectual curiosity.
As we mark this significant milestone in the school’s history, we look forward to welcoming pupils into these exceptional new spaces and the opportunities they will create for generations to come.
Please explore our digital brochure to learn more and see images that bring these exciting developments to life.
To see these exciting developments first-hand, we invite you to join us at our Whole School Open Morning on Saturday 26th September. I look forward to welcoming you and sharing our vision for the future of Babington as we begin the new academic year.
Whether you’re exploring options for Nursery, Prep, or Senior School, this is the perfect opportunity to discover everything that makes Babington House so special.

Our Nursery children benefit from the expertise of fully qualified teachers from the very beginning of their school journey.
Our carefully considered approach combines nurturing care and play-based learning with purposeful academic preparation, encouraging children to become confident, curious and independent learners.
Through engaging experiences and age-appropriate challenge, we build the foundations for a successful start to school, ensuring a smooth and seamless transition into Reception and a strong foundation for the years beyond.
Physical Education
Our Nursery and Reception pupils enjoy weekly PE lessons where they have fun, learn new skills and develop their physical health.
In addition, our Nursery and Reception pupils benefit from a new bespoke outdoor area featuring an obstacle course where children can develop physical, practical and communication skills through play and exploration.
Music
Music is taught by a specialist teacher at Babington House School, giving our youngest children the opportunity to develop a love of music from the very beginning of their school journey. Through singing, rhythm, movement, musical exploration and instrument playing, children develop their listening, memory, coordination and confidence, while learning to express themselves creatively.
Our new bespoke outdoor area extends these opportunities with a dedicated stage, where children can sing, perform and share their ideas with others. These experiences nurture confident communicators, encouraging children to find their voice, enjoy performing and embrace new challenges in a supportive and inspiring environment.
Languages
At Babington, languages are introduced in the Early Years. The children enjoy weekly lessons in French and Spanish where they develop simple vocabulary through songs and practical activities.
Outdoor learning
Our Nursery children enjoy Bushcraft sessions, while Reception children take part in Forest School, providing exciting opportunities to explore, discover and learn in the natural environment. These experiences encourage children to develop confidence, independence and resilience as they learn to take considered risks, solve problems and work collaboratively.
Our new bespoke outdoor area further enriches this learning, with dedicated spaces designed to inspire curiosity, creativity and practical skills. Children can nurture and harvest their own vegetables in our garden, develop fine motor skills and concentration through woodwork, and enjoy imaginative play in our water, sand and mud kitchen areas.
Through these purposeful experiences, children are encouraged to experiment, create, problem-solve and work together, building the confidence and skills they need to thrive as enthusiastic, capable learners.

pageCache.pageTitle: Careers | Private School London | Babington House
pageCache.text:
Preparation for futures after Babington House is an integral part of our student’s journey. The careers provision follows the 8 Gatsby Benchmarks ensuring the school provides a wholistic careers programme for students.
Further information can be found here.
Please contact our Careers Lead is Mrs Paterson, epaterson@babingtonhouse.com telephone 0208 467 5537 Ext 300.
“Preparing and empowering our students; encouraging them to grow into valued members of our community and enabling them to gain and sustain enriched futures.”
Unifrog
The Unifrog platform is available to all KS3, KS4 & KS5 students and their families and is an integral part of the careers programme. It can be used to support student’s future plans including post 16 & 18 pathways, exploring interests, completing skills quizzes, investigating universities, studying abroad, apprenticeships and colleges, deep dives into job sectors, attend live webinars, and much more.
Every senior student has a Unifrog account linked to their school email address.
Families can request login information by emailing Mrs Paterson (epaterson@babingtonhouse.com).
Work Experience
“More than 80% of young people felt they were more attractive to employers following work experience or an employer-led placement and around 75% of work experience participants said it had provided them with new skills and increased their confidence”
Work experience is completed by students in years 10 for one week during the summer term. This year’s dates are: 29th June to 3rd July 2026.
If you can offer a work placement in the future to one of our students, please contact Mrs Paterson (Epaterson@babingtonhouse.com)
Timely support
As well as regular careers sessions, students are supported at crucial times when important decisions must be made, this includes choosing their GCSE options in Year 9 and deciding on post 16 and post 18 plans.
Our Independent Careers Adviser Kirsty Taylor will have a 1 to 1 meeting with students at relevant times to ensure they have the correct tools to make informed choices about their futures.

pageCache.pageTitle: Enrichment | Private School London | Babington House
pageCache.text:
Enrichment programme
We are proud to offer a broad and inspiring Enrichment Programme for pupils in Years 3–8, taking place once a week within the school day alongside the core curriculum. The programme provides pupils with exciting opportunities to discover new interests, develop their talents and build confidence beyond the classroom. With a varied range of activities including musical theatre, mathematical thinking, music technology, sport, dance, debating, digital development and AI, and Forest School, there is something to inspire every pupil.
At Babington House, we are also proud of our strong links with the local community. Through our Enrichment Programme, pupils have the opportunity to volunteer with local initiatives, including supporting Elmstead Woods Station and visiting residents at a local care home, helping them to develop empathy, responsibility and a genuine sense of community.

pageCache.pageTitle: Pastoral Care | Private School London | Babington House
pageCache.text:
At Babington House we actively promote the wellbeing of all our students. This includes ensuring their physical, mental health and emotional wellbeing are at the forefront of all that we do. From the moment a child joins our Nursery through to the day they leave us, every pupil is known, valued and supported as an individual. Our small class sizes, close-knit community and dedicated pastoral team mean no child is ever just a face in the crowd. Each one is known by name, by personality, and by the things that make them who they are. It is this depth of knowledge, and the trusted relationships built day after day, that allows us to nurture happy, confident children who feel safe, settled and ready to learn.
Nurturing Bright Minds
At Babington House School we believe in the importance of valuing all children, regardless of their abilities or difficulties. Providing a broad and balanced curriculum which is differentiated to meet individual needs, that enables all children to reach their potential through effective teaching.
We recognise that every child is wonderfully unique, and that academic progress goes hand in hand with emotional and social development. Our form teachers, supported by our Qualified Teaching Assistants and wider pastoral team, take the time to understand each pupil: how they learn, how they feel, where they shine and where they need a little extra encouragement. This careful, personal attention means that children are not only supported through challenges, but genuinely celebrated for the individuals they are.
Watch Our School Film
Where next

We are extremely proud of our academic success and reputation, and we celebrate all our students’ personal achievements. Whilst Grade 9’s are wonderful, we believe the true value of a Babington education is found in those individuals who achieve a grade (or two) higher than they ever thought possible, or in a pupil who didn’t believe they could, who now knows they can.
GCSE results 2026
We are delighted to celebrate the outstanding achievements of our Year 11 students on GCSE Results Day.
This year marks a significant leap forward in our top grades, with over half of all students achieving grades 9–7 across a wide range of subjects. Outstanding results were achieved in subjects including Biology, French, Further Maths, Fine Art, Textiles and 3D Design.
Over a third of all students achieved 9-7 grades in English Language, English Literature, Mathematics, Chemistry, Physics, Computer Science, Spanish, Drama, and Physical Education highlighting the vast array of outstanding ability of Babington House students in literary based, STEM, and creative subjects.
Most notably, nearly twice as many of our students achieved the highest grades of 9–7 compared with the national average, reflecting the exceptional commitment, determination and resilience demonstrated by our students throughout their GCSE journey.
These results are a testament to the hard work of our students, the encouragement and support of their families, and the dedication of our teaching and support staff. We are immensely proud of the achievements of the Year 11 cohort and the progress they have made during their time at Babington.
Our students will now take their next steps at a range of grammar, independent and local schools, and we wish every one of them continued success as they begin the next chapter of their education.
Congratulations to the Class of 2026 — we are incredibly proud of you and look forward to seeing all that you achieve in the future.
*Results based on 39 pupils.
A Level Results 2026
Congratulations to all our A Level students on achieving a fantastic set of results which marks the end of two years of hard work and dedication, we are delighted with the plethora of top university places that Babington House students have successfully secured.
The unique range of skills and talents that have been nurtured and developed during students’ time at Babington are evidenced in the broad range of ambitious Undergraduate courses that students have successfully secured. A number of our students are going on to study courses centred in STEM subjects, such as Veterinary Science, Neuroscience, Psychology, Sport Science, Computer Games Design and Computer Animation. Additionally, a number who have excelled in the creative subjects are going on to pursue their artistic skills in creative subjects including Hair, Make-Up and Prosthetics for Performance at the University of the Arts London.
Many are choosing to pursue courses with real-world application and developing skills for a successful future in business, including Management and Marketing, Economics, Finance and International Relations, whilst some students will pursue their ambitions to study real world application of theories and structures through studying Anthropology and Politics.
We know that they have grown and developed into confident young people during their time with us, ambitious for their futures, and equipped to rise to the challenges of whatever life throws at them. We wish them all the very best.
*Results based on 22 pupils.

pageCache.pageTitle: Senior Curriculum | Senior School London | Babington House
pageCache.text:
View our GCSE Options Booklet:
English
The English department at Babington House plays a key role within the school. We aim to stimulate intellectual, emotional, social and academic growth. In addition, lessons expose pupils to different and often conflicting viewpoints, develop pupils’ speaking and listening skills and helping to foster a life-long love for reading and learning.
In Years 7 – 9 we begin to prepare students for the skills they will need at GCSE level. This covers three strands:
We use Assessment for Learning extensively and pupils are part of their own learning with individual, peer and teacher assessments completed regularly. All our pupils are entered for both English Language and English Literature GCSEs, following the AQA specifications for examination.
The requirements of the new GCSE mean that students no longer complete Controlled Assessments for GCSE English Literature and Language, and all exams are taken at the end of Year 11.
In Years 10 and 11 we prepare students for the following examinations:
English Literature: Paper 1: Shakespeare and the 19th Century Novel Paper 2: Modern texts and Poetry
English Language: Paper 1: Explorations in Creative Reading and Writing Paper 2: Writers’ Viewpoints and Perspectives
Spoken Language Non-Examination Assessment – separate endorsement (0% weighting of GCSE)
In addition, we widely encourage reading and have a book-borrowing scheme within the department. Our debating club is run by pupils in Year 11 and gives the girls the opportunity to work with other year groups and express their views in a safe and rewarding environment.
The department seeks to encourage and extend an enjoyment, appreciation and understanding of both English Language and English Literature and create an atmosphere where students wish to learn.
Speaking and Listening
Mathematics
Welcome to Mathematics. This innovative department is focussed on the pupils’ learning and achievements. We work to ensure that every pupil has the opportunity and encouragement to do their very best, to develop mathematical thinking, to raise standards and to enjoy mathematics.
All pupils follow a linear Mathematics course, starting in Year 7, that eventually leads to the Edexcel GCSE examination. Each year group is divided by ability into two sets (KS3) and then three sets (KS4) enabling them to be challenged according to their ability.
Students in Years 10 and 11 are offered the opportunity to study GCSE Further Maths as well as GCSE Maths. Further Maths is a great way to stretch our most able Mathematicians, giving them a taste of more advanced Mathematics particularly if they are considering studying Maths at A Level and beyond.
GCSE Mathematics is designed to equip students with fluent knowledge, skills and understanding of mathematical methods and concepts. On completion of the course, students will be able to reason mathematically, draw conclusions and interpret mathematical information in a variety of forms.
Mathematics provides a strong foundation for employment and further academic and vocational study. The knowledge and skills obtained by students at GCSE level will help them to progress to a full range of courses in higher education and are crucial in other disciplines such as biology, physics and geography.

Science
Exploring ecosystems, microorganisms, stars, particle accelerators and launching rockets into space are just a few of the exciting possibilities offered to students by our outstanding Science department at Babington House.
Science is taught at Key Stage 3-4 in three purpose-built, fully resourced science laboratories. In science, our aim is to provide an excellent education for all our students, giving them the knowledge and skills they need to understand the world around them.
At Key Stage 3 we follow the AQA Activate course. This has been specifically tailored to the new AQA KS3 Syllabus and Big Ideas principle and helps students prepare for AQA GCSE Sciences which we follow at KS4. All students get free online access to the student eBooks and resources via Kerboodle.
In Year’s 7 and 8, students have two science lessons each week covering the following topics:
Movement, Cells, Interdependence, Plant and human reproduction, Variation.
Particle model, Separating mixtures, Acids and alkalis, Metals and non-metals, The Earth and Universe.
Speed, Gravity, Electrical circuits, Energy costs and transfer, Sound and Light.
Breathing, Digestion, Respiration, Photosynthesis, Evolution, Inheritance.
Elements, The Periodic Table, Types of reactions, Chemical energy, Climate and Earth resources
Forces and pressure, Magnetism, Electromagnetism, Work, Heating and cooling, Wave effects and properties.
At KS4, we follow the AQA specification for GCSE Sciences. All students get free online access to the student eBooks via Boost (the online platform provided by Hodder Education).
In Year 9 students begin preparing for their GCSE courses and are taught the three sciences, Biology, Chemistry and Physics, as separate subjects by specialist teachers. At the end of Year 9, pupils will then choose to study either Combined Science (equivalent to two GCSE’s) or Triple Sciences (equivalent to three GCSE’s).
GCSE Combined Science: Trilogy AQA (8464) Combined Science is a course with a wide-ranging curriculum that encompasses all three sciences and will suit students with any scientific aspiration. The course aims to encourage students to develop a critical approach to scientific evidence, develop the scientific literacy needed by every citizen as well as explore the implications of science for society.
By the end of the course students will have gained a knowledge and understanding of science and how science works, applied their skills of knowledge and understanding to new situations, and developed their practical, enquiry and data handling skills.
Summary of the scheme of assessment: At the end of Year 11, students will sit two examinations for each science (six in total). Each paper contains multiple choice, structured, closed, short answer and open response questions. There is no coursework component for this course. Instead, there are a number of required practicals that students must carry out throughout the course. These will be assessed in the terminal examination.
GCSE Triple Sciences in Biology, Chemistry and Physics Each GCSE above acts as a stand-alone qualification. Students studying Biology, Chemistry and Physics as separate sciences will cover more content than GCSE Combined Science which will provide greater preparation for KS5.
Summary of the scheme of assessment: For each science students will sit two examinations. Again, each paper contains multiple choice, structured, closed, short answer and open response questions. There is no coursework component for this course. Instead, there are a number of required practicals that students must carry out throughout the course. These will be assessed in the terminal examination.
Art, Textiles & Product Design
The Art Department at Babington is a thriving, dynamic area within the curriculum that constantly evolves to reflect current exhibitions and art practice. Fine Art, Textile Design and Product Design are taught from year 7 to year 9, with courses offered at GCSE.
In years 7, 8 and 9 pupils study a broad range of skills and techniques. Some of the areas covered are still-life, perspective, printing and painting. Pupils learn to weave, make felt, knit, stitch by hand and machine and generally design work to be translated into fabric. They also learn cutting skills, construction methods and designing to meet specific criteria. At all stages a multi-cultural approach is taken with an emphasis on experimentation and historical reference.
For GCSE a portfolio of work is developed, refined and modified with a strong emphasis on independent learning. Preparation for the exam is undertaken over several weeks.
Economics and Business Studies
Business directs and drives the world economy. It provides employment and leisure and generates income and wealth. Business helps to improve our quality of life and provides both essential and luxurious goods and services.
GCSE Economics at Babington offers students the chance to explore fascinating real-world issues, from how businesses make decisions to why economies grow and how governments respond to economic challenges. It is an excellent opportunity for students to develop skills that will support them both academically and beyond the classroom.
Business is available from Key Stage 4. Studying a range of real-life business scenarios students will look at their impact on decision making and develop an understanding of business concepts, objectives and terminology, gaining an understanding of the impact of internal and external issues and how they affect business operations.
Students will explore the purpose and role of a business from identifying a gap in the market through to business planning and delivery. How marketing plays a role in identifying and satisfying customer needs and why a strong human resource management structure plays an important role in supporting a business right the way through the process. Operations and Finance will be key areas of learning, looking at how businesses respond to external market forces, such as ethical and environmental considerations, the economic climate and globalisation.
Computer Science
Computer Science in Key Stage 3, 4 and 5 at Babington House equips pupils to become inquisitive programmers, using computational thinking and creativity to understand and change the world. Computing has deep links with mathematics, science, and design and technology. It provides insights into both natural and artificial systems.
The core of computing is computer science, in which pupils are taught the principles of information and computation, how digital systems work, and how to put this knowledge to use through programming. Building on this knowledge and understanding, students are equipped to use information technology to create programs, systems and a range of content. Computing also ensures that pupils become digitally literate – able to use, and express themselves and develop their ideas through, information and communication technology – at a level suitable for the future workplace and as active participants in a digital world. Pupils wishing to develop their skills further can choose Computer Science as an option at GCSE and A level.
Dance
Our Dance Department aims to provide a safe, fun, inclusive and high-quality environment where every student can develop confidence, creativity and a love of dance.
Our curriculum is built around the three key principles of Create, Perform and Appreciate, giving students opportunities to develop their fitness, dance technique, performance and choreography skills, while broadening their knowledge and appreciation of dance as an art form.
Through structured lessons, students will explore a diverse range of styles, including street dance techniques, dance through the decades, dance from around the world, musical theatre and contemporary dance, alongside learning about influential choreographers and practitioners and dance on our screens.
Dance offers students a unique opportunity to be creative, expressive and physically active, while developing valuable skills in teamwork, communication and confidence.
Drama
The Drama Department offers students a dynamic platform to delve into and engage with a diverse array of dramatic styles and genres. With an ever-present drive to learn and embrace new influences, the curriculum fosters both personal and artistic growth.
Key Stage 3 (Years 7-9) At Key Stage 3, Drama plays a pivotal role in enriching the broader curriculum while simultaneously cultivating essential creative and teamwork abilities. It is also instrumental in building confidence and enhancing social skills. During these formative years, Drama lessons focus on developing:
GCSE Drama As students advance to GCSE level, they are challenged to deepen their creative abilities, collaborate effectively to produce captivating performances, and refine their verbal and written evaluation skills. The course follows the Eduqas specification and is divided into three units:
Annual School Production Each year, Babington House stages a major school production, offering students the chance to engage in all aspects of theatre. From acting and stage design to lighting, backstage management, costumes, and makeup, this eagerly anticipated event aims to involve as many students as possible, providing a comprehensive experience in theatrical production.
Practitioner Work: Exploring practitioner’s techniques
Devising Theatre (Teacher Assessed)
Performing from a Text (Externally Assessed)
Interpreting Theatre (Final Exam, Externally Assessed)
Geography
Geography is an active and engaging subject at Babington House School. Teaching and learning is based upon a successful mixture of skills, knowledge and concepts with a strong emphasis placed on students developing independence and leadership of their own learning.
At Key Stage 3 all students study Geography as part of the curriculum. Typically, this would include the investigation of the weather and Climate to understand climate change, the processes affecting the coast and the impact of flooding. The curriculum is current and focuses on real life events in order to help students make sense of the world around them, for instance studying the factors and processes those natural disasters and the impact and responses of the human population.

pageCache.pageTitle: Welcome To Early Years | Babington House
pageCache.text:
From the very first day they join us, our youngest children become valued members of our vibrant whole-school community. Within our warm, nurturing and stimulating Nursery environment, every child is encouraged to develop confidence, curiosity and a genuine love of learning.
Our newly refurbished Early Years classrooms have been thoughtfully designed to create bespoke, welcoming spaces where children feel safe, happy and inspired. Carefully planned indoor and outdoor learning environments provide countless opportunities for exploration, creativity and discovery, supporting every stage of a child’s development.
At the heart of our Nursery is a belief that children learn best when they are actively engaged in their own learning. Through play-based experiences and expert guidance from our dedicated Early Years team, children learn to ask questions, solve problems, take appropriate risks and work collaboratively with others. We celebrate individuality while encouraging independence, resilience and kindness.
Being part of an all-through school offers unique opportunities from the very beginning. Nursery children enjoy becoming part of the wider school family, benefiting from specialist teaching and experiences that enrich their learning. Weekly language lessons introduce them to new cultures and ways of communicating, while music lessons foster creativity and self-expression
Every day is filled with laughter, discovery and achievement. Our Nursery is a place where children are known as individuals, celebrated for their successes and supported to reach their full potential. It is a happy environment characterised by care, positivity and a strong sense of belonging.
We warmly invite you to visit and experience our Nursery for yourself. Whether you join us for a stay-and-play session or a personal tour, we would be delighted to welcome you and show you what makes our Early Years provision such a special place to begin a child’s educational journey.
Mrs Elizabeth Channon
Head of Nursery and Prep

pageCache.pageTitle: Nursery Stay and Discover | Babington House
pageCache.text:
Our Stay & Discover sessions are a wonderful way for young children and their families to experience the warmth and creativity of Early Years at Babington House School. Designed especially for children aged 2–4, these sessions are led by our experienced Early Years staff, who create a fun, welcoming and relaxed environment for everyone to enjoy.
Each session is filled with age-appropriate activities that spark curiosity, encourage creativity and introduce children to the joy of learning through play. It’s also a lovely chance for parents to meet our specialist team, ask questions and see how we nurture every child’s early development.
Whether it’s exploring new toys, enjoying stories, or taking part in imaginative play, children will have the opportunity to feel comfortable in our classrooms and begin building confidence in a school setting. Parents can also get a real sense of the caring, family-focused ethos that makes Babington such a special place to start their educational journey.
We look forward to welcoming you and your child to one of our sessions and sharing a taste of the exciting adventures that await in our Nursery.

Welcome to Prep
Our school is a vibrant and nurturing community where every child is known, valued and encouraged to achieve their very best. We believe that academic excellence and outstanding pastoral care go hand in hand, creating an environment in which children feel confident, happy and ready to thrive.
At the heart of everything we do are our core values of kindness, respect, honesty, determination and courtesy. These principles guide daily life across the school and help to foster a culture where children develop not only as successful learners, but also as thoughtful and compassionate individuals. We hold high expectations for all members of our community, and this shared commitment enables our school to remain a warm, welcoming and inclusive place for everyone.
In the Prep, we strive to nurture a genuine love of learning. We encourage children to be curious, ask questions, take risks and view mistakes as valuable opportunities for growth. Through an engaging curriculum, extensive enrichment opportunities and a wide range of co-curricular activities, every child is given the chance to discover their talents, pursue their interests and develop the confidence to embrace new challenges.
We want our pupils to approach each day with enthusiasm, resilience and a sense of adventure. By encouraging them to explore, create and dream big, we help them build the skills and character they need to flourish both now and in the future.
I am immensely proud to lead such a caring and ambitious school community. I warmly invite you to visit us, meet our pupils and staff, and experience for yourself the unique atmosphere that makes our school such a special place. I look forward to welcoming you.
Mrs Elizabeth Channon
